newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian bourse releases short-sale stock list.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian bourse releases short-sale stock list.

text.p: The Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE) on Friday released a list of 50 approved stocks permitted to be sold short.
Short selling of securities will be allowed starting on Monday. Under the practice, an investor sells securities he does not own in the hope of replacing them at lower prices.

The number of stocks approved is higher than the 20-30 stocks that the exchange earlier indicated would be on the list. Because of strict criteria, market regulators had indicated that only the strongest capitalised, most liquid stocks would be short-sale candidates.

The criteria for approval included an average daily market capitalisation of over 2 billion ringgit for the past three months, at least 100 million shares in public float, at least 2,000 registered shareholders, five years uninterrupted after-tax profit record and average monthly share volume trade of more than two million shares for the past 12 calendar months.

Just about all the top 20 biggest capitalised companies in Malaysia made the list, with the notable exceptions of Malaysia International Shipping Corp Bhd (MISC), Rothmans of Pall Mall (Malaysia) Bhd, which is the subsidiary of the U.K. tobacco concern; container shipping concern PDZ Holdings Bhd and car distributor Edaran Otomobil Nasional Bhd.

Otherwise, the list encompasses the biggest names in Malaysia's stock market including national airline Malaysian Airline System Bhd (MAS), as well as giant telephone utility Telekom Malaysia Bhd and state-controlled electric utility Tenaga Nasional Bhd.
Banks and financial services firms formed the biggest contingent on the list, with 13 representatives.
KLSE officials were not available for queries about the list make-up. The exchange said in a statement that the list was "as agreed by the Securities Commission."
Under the KLSE's rules, only stockbrokers which have in-place exchange-approved written guidelines on 'know your customer practices' will be permitted to engage in regulated shortselling.
The guidelines include apprising customers of the risks involved, and making sure the clients can meet their financial commitments.
